witnesses.reason: Condition 6(a) on PDF page 106 states maturity redemption at the final redemption amount, defaulting to nominal amount. The selected final terms page 5 supplies EUR100,000 per EUR100,000 denomination. Earlier Renminbi interest text in the quotation is unrelated and does not determine repayment.

Final terms page 5 item 22 expressly equates EUR100,000 final redemption to EUR100,000 denomination. Item 9/page 3 and item 27/page 6 exclude instalments. This is conditional scheduled principal repayment, not evidence of all-law safety.
Condition 6(c) defines make-whole optional redemption at least at nominal principal. Final terms page 4 item 16 selects this option; the holder does not acquire an unconditional put.

UNSUPPORTED: Condition 7(f) addresses deduction for missing coupons of materialised bearer notes; selected issue page 6 is dematerialised. Mere proximity of Final Redemption Amount and Amortised Nominal Amount is neither selected repayment nor a principal equality.

UNSUPPORTED as a principal-repayment witness: the first sentence lists meanings of principal including Amortised Nominal Amount, without an equality or amount promise. The following event-of-default acceleration is conditional and does not turn those definitions into full principal repayment. The lexical matcher incorrectly linked Final Redemption Amounts to Nominal Amounts.

Condition 6.1 pages 115-116 explicitly requires irrevocable mandatory conversion without holder consent when the defined CET1 Trigger Event occurs. Common Shares are ordinary shares (page 1). Condition 6.2/page 117 opt-out applies to Capital Reduction Conversion, not this Trigger Conversion; its last paragraph preserves 6.1.
Page 31 describes Trigger Event conversion, corroborated by Condition 6.1, without holder consent. This does not include the separate capital-reduction election route.

Page 1 expressly conditions ordinary-share conversion on the Bank or Group CET1 ratio below 5.125%, as determined by the Bank. Preserve the conversion price floor and nominal-value conditions; no actual trigger or share quantity established.

Page 45 overview follows the CET1 threshold on the same page and names a Trigger Event; Conditions 6.1 and the page 1 Common Shares definition corroborate its mandatory ordinary-share conversion. The fragment alone is insufficient without that surrounding definition.

Condition 5A.02(i) expressly reduces principal to zero on the conversion date. Conditions 5A.01 and 5A.02(iv), pages 39-40, tie that reduction to automatic trigger conversion and remaining share-delivery rights. It is a principal extinguishment in exchange for shares, not a separate unconditional confiscation or established 100% economic loss.

Page 5 names ordinary-share conversion risk for these notes. Pages 39-40 require automatic conversion with no holder approval and define resulting settlement rights; page 59 defines Conversion Shares as Class A Shares. This supports the conditional feature without establishing an actual event.

Page 13 expressly couples principal reduction to zero with trigger conversion and the remaining share-delivery obligation. Conditions 5A.01-5A.02 corroborate this. The classification does not mean shares or sale proceeds have zero value.
